No network operations, script executions, or file modifications are present in the file—only declarative source and dependency metadata.

The dependencies and optional dependencies are consistent with the application's functionality—an OBS Studio plugin requiring networking, multimedia, and automation features. Nothing in the file indicates data exfiltration, remote code execution, or unauthorized system access. The file adheres to standard AUR packaging practices and shows no signs of tampering or injected malicious logic.

The provided file `FindTesseract.cmake` is a CMake module script used to locate and configure the Tesseract OCR library during the build process. It follows standard CMake practices for finding dependencies via `pkg-config`, locating header files and libraries, handling debug/release variants, and setting up imported targets. The script checks for Tesseract using `pkg_check_modules`, searches for include directories and libraries, and properly sets up the `Tesseract::Tesseract` target with appropriate properties.

It also integrates with Leptonica, a known dependency of Tesseract, by requiring it and linking it via `target_link_libraries`. All operations are limited to configuring build system variables and targets—there are no network operations, file modifications outside build configuration, execution of external scripts, or use of dangerous commands like `eval`, `curl`, or `bash`. The use of `add_library` and `set_target_properties` is normal CMake functionality and not indicative of malicious behavior.

The code is consistent with upstream CMake Find modules and serves only to integrate Tesseract into a CMake-based build system. There is no obfuscation, unexpected system interaction, or data exfiltration.
</details>

These modifications are typical in Arch packaging to ensure compatibility with system libraries and modern Qt versions. There are no obfuscated commands, suspicious downloads, or unauthorized network operations. The build uses standard `cmake` procedures, and installation targets `$pkgdir` safely.

No evidence of supply-chain attacks, backdoors, or data exfiltration mechanisms was found. All operations align with expected packaging behavior for an AUR package. While the `cpp-httplib` source lacks a checksum and tracks the main branch (an unpinned, mutable reference), this is not uncommon for actively developed C++ header-only libraries and does not rise to the level of a security threat on its own.
